title: Who chose the default?
hook: Would you read a preselected option as advice or as convenience?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Distinguish perceived recommendation from mechanical effort when interpreting a default.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Distinguish perceived recommendation from mechanical effort when interpreting a default.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: A toy default saves one click in both cases. Only one default is described as a recommendation. How many clicks does the recommendation itself save? Toy inputs A=[1, 1, 0]; B=[1, 0, 1].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[1, 0, 1], [1, 0, 0]]. Labels: Shortcut clicks, Extra clicks, Advice cue.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: The mechanical shortcut is held constant while the stated origin changes. This isolates a recommendation cue from click effort in the toy design; it does not establish how strongly either cue affects real choices.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Saved clicks=1, Recommendation=0, Random rule=1. What is Extra clicks? Answer: 0.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Saved clicks=1, Recommendation=0, Random rule=1. What is Extra clicks?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 0. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: People read defaults as an implicit recommendation from whoever set them (McKenzie, Liersch & Finkelstein, 2006).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Distinguish perceived recommendation from mechanical effort when interpreting a default.
